panels.title: Requests per second
panels.description: Laravel requests by status class. The metrics and health endpoints are left out.

panels.title: Response time
panels.description: Time Laravel spends on a request, from the first middleware to the response.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Share of requests answered with a client or server error.

panels.title: Response time distribution
panels.description: How many requests landed in each response time bucket.

panels.title: Slowest routes (p95, last 5 minutes)
panels.description: Routes with traffic in the last five minutes, ranked by their 95th percentile response time.

defaults.noValue: No traffic in the last 5 minutes

panels.title: Routes (last 5 minutes)
panels.description: Traffic, response time and error share per route. Only routes with requests in the last five minutes are listed.

targets.expr: (sum by (route) (rate(app_http_requests_total{status_code=~"[45].."}[5m])) or sum by (route) (rate(app_http_requests_total[5m])) * 0) / sum by (route) (rate(app_http_requests_total[5m]))

defaults.noValue: No traffic in the last 5 minutes

panels.title: Caddy requests per second
panels.description: Everything the public site served, including static assets and the Grafana proxy.

panels.title: Caddy response time
panels.description: PHP requests as Caddy sees them, including time spent waiting for a free thread. Static files and the Grafana proxy are left out.

panels.title: PHP threads
panels.description: FrankenPHP threads handling requests. Queued requests means every thread was busy.

panels.title: Server CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the FrankenPHP process, where 100% is one full core.

panels.title: Metrics scrape duration
panels.description: How long Prometheus takes to collect each target. Anything near the scrape interval leaves gaps in the graphs.
